videos.title: Apple, AMD, Palantir Lead Big Earnings Week

findings.summary: Two IBD hosts (Rachel Fox and Ed Carson) preview a slate of upcoming earnings reports, covering Apple, AMD, Palantir, and about a dozen other names. The discussion is mostly technical chart commentary (buy zones, moving-average levels, relative strength) paired with consensus EPS and revenue expectations and year-over-year growth figures. Hosts make no explicit guaranteed-return claims, but they lean on chart-pattern language and repeatedly say a stock is "extended" or wait for a buy point. No position disclosure was given.
findings.macro_points: ["Midterm elections fall around the same days as several reports and are described as an added market risk.", "Software sector has been volatile, with some sharp down days.", "AI stocks are described as out of favor recently, while consumer-facing tech is seen as well positioned.", "Hosts say the broader market has struggled to make progress while some individual names keep rising.", "Hosts say investors will get a read on AI-related CPU demand from Intel's earnings shortly before AMD reports."]
red_flags: Heavy reliance on chart-pattern and buy-point language with little discussion of valuation or downside risk
Hosts say several names are extended above key moving averages (e.g., ShakeNinja and GRAIL-type names described as 42% above the 50-day), which raises chasing risk
Several names described as 'fake-out' breakouts or choppy and hard to trade
Hosts discuss speculative hot-sector names, including unprofitable diagnostics and cancer-testing firms, with little risk framing
Mentions of M&A rumor affecting Lumentum's price action, without verification
No discussion of downside scenarios or position sizing; many forward-looking remarks about post-earnings moves are speculative

tickers.thesis: Hosts expect fiscal Q4 consensus EPS near $1.99 and revenue near $113.4B, with growth slowing from recent acceleration. They view the stock as acting well and near a buy zone, and see the new CEO's first call and iPhone and services revenue as key watch items.

Hosts expect consensus EPS near $1.95 (about 62% growth) and revenue near $13.09B (about 42% growth), and see AI data center and CPU demand as drivers. They describe the stock as technically strong and possibly actionable above a prior buy point of 584, but the outlook depends heavily on AI spending holding up.

Hosts expect adjusted EPS near $0.41 and revenue near $2.18B, with US commercial revenue as the key metric. They note a long run of accelerating growth, a strong accumulation rating, and a resilient chart, but say they would wait until after earnings and the election.

findings.summary: A podcast interview with Alex Altman, head of tactical equity strategies at Barclays (the "Bets" team), on market positioning, retail ownership, and AI-related financing. He argues the market is tactically bearish for the next several weeks, citing a quant timing model, crowded positioning, heavy equity issuance, and tighter credit spreads for AI data-center debt, while noting the hyperscalers have so far been resilient. The episode also includes off-topic banter about Manhattan neighborhoods and the host's nickname.
macro_points: Equity net issuance is expected to turn positive in 2026 for the first time in a long while, as IPOs and at-the-money offerings rise while buybacks stay roughly flat.
Competition for capital: projected 2026 net investment-grade and high-yield issuance of about $1.2 trillion, with spreads on AI data-center debt widening.
US household equity ownership and the share of household net worth in stocks are described as at or near record highs, with 401k inflows described as a steady buying source.
Retail and passive/systematic flows are described as a volatility dampener, and the speaker argues the stock market now drives the economy via the wealth effect.
AI capex is described as consuming a large share of hyperscaler revenue, with the speaker questioning how the spending will be covered by revenue.
Index-level correlation among S&P 500 stocks is described as unusually low, with relative-value and multi-manager pod crowding cited as a cause.
red_flags: Tactical short-term market calls presented without any stated track record or hit rate for the speaker's own calls; the host admits the framework is 'not perfect'.
Proprietary quant model (Betty) and client survey results are cited but not shown in full, so claims are hard to verify independently.
Speaker claims a 2026 AI revenue gap of roughly a trillion dollars without showing the underlying model in detail.
Speculation about a possible Nvidia rescue of CoreWeave and a broad AI unwind is presented as a scenario, not a forecast with evidence.

Speaker is affiliated with Barclays and discusses Barclays' own research products; the interview ends with a mention of institutional research access, which is mildly promotional but not a paid pitch.

videos.title: Gilead Sciences Q3 FY26 Earnings Call | $GILD | 🔴 WATCH LIVE

findings.summary: Gilead's Q3 2026 earnings call (partial transcript, ends mid-prepared remarks). Management reported base business sales up 16% year-over-year, with HIV (Biktarvy, Yeztugo, Sunlenca-type prep products), Trodelvy and Livdelzi driving growth, and said it raised 2026 base business revenue guidance by $1.6 billion. Management also discussed pipeline milestones (oral and injectable HIV regimens, Trodelvy endometrial data, inflammation programs) and said the Medicare maximum fair price for Biktarvy takes effect in 2028. The transcript is auto-generated and partly garbled, so some product and drug names are uncertain.
macro_points: Management said the CMS maximum fair price process for Biktarvy is complete and will affect McTar/Biktarvy revenue in 2028 (the transcript is garbled here; the drug name is uncertain).
Management said the HIV treatment market has not yet returned to its typical 2-3% growth but shows signs of stabilization.
Management said the US PrEP market grew 14% year-over-year in the quarter.
red_flags: Earnings call from a company, not an independent analyst; management is presenting its own results and guidance.
Management said some Q3 HIV and Discovy growth came from favorable inventory dynamics, which it expects to normalize by year end.
Cell therapy (Kite) sales fell 18% year-over-year, which management attributed to competitive headwinds.
Policy headwind: Medicare price-setting will hit a key product's revenue starting 2028; the price figure itself was not stated in the portion transcribed.
Many pipeline outcomes are described as future events (filings, data readouts, approvals), so their success is not yet established.

tickers.thesis: Management describes the strongest base business growth in over a decade, driven by HIV, Trodelvy and Livdelzi, and says diversification and a broad pipeline support durable growth. Management raised 2026 base business revenue guidance by $1.6 billion. Management is the source of these claims; the call is not an independent assessment.
tickers.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings; upcoming Yeztugo once-weekly oral PrEP FDA decision in early Feb 2027; Anito-cel (anitocabtagene autoleucel) approval expected by end of 2026; Trodelvy ASCENT-GU phase 3 update around year end
